summary: Preserve integrated legacy worktrees during first native adoption

delivery.outcome: Permit first native adoption while preserving clean canonical legacy worktrees at strictly integrated commits; retain exact admission and publication boundaries.
nonGoals: No legacy checkout/ref deletion, repair, ownership transfer or lease changes
No target-specific tickets or logs in the standard hub
No publication bypass or unpublished production adoption

architecture.decision: Share a read-only canonical-worktree observation between initial admission and receipt refresh; require strict ancestry, clean state, exact Git bindings and stable repeated observations. Existing historical lease and native reservation checks remain mandatory.
interfaceChanges: Additional preserved canonical worktrees can satisfy first-allocation observation
architecture.rollback: Revert through independent protected publication; no legacy state is mutated by observation.

validation.evidence: Real first allocation preserves integrated canonical checkout and rejects dirty, ambiguous, detached, noncanonical and live-leased work.
Receipt refresh uses the same preserved-worktree boundaries and refuses observation drift.
Native governance, package parity, exact-head required CI, independent Validator and immutable published release before adoption.
